findings.title: question and negation are compressed
findings.claim: The fused {ar:أَلَمْ, tr:alam, gloss:bilmez mi} makes the opening a single accusatory challenge.
findings.mechanism: The interrogative hamza and jussive negation share one surface unit and govern the following knowing verb, turning absent knowledge into an immediate examination.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah enters as an abrupt rebuke rather than a neutral request for information.
findings.containment: The ordinary negative-interrogative force remains primary; its compressed rhetorical pressure is the added finding.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology, syntax, sound, or local relation directly supports the bounded finding.

findings.title: seeing-question pattern turns into knowledge rebuke
findings.claim: The earlier seeing-question register is reworked here as a question about knowing that God sees.
findings.mechanism: The local {ar:يَعْلَمْ, tr:yaʿlam, gloss:bilir} follows {ar:أَلَمْ, tr:alam, gloss:bilmez mi} and receives the {ar:بِأَنَّ ... يَرَىٰ, tr:bi-anna ... yarā, gloss:Allah'ın gördüğü} content, creating a structural echo without identical wording.
findings.reader_payoff: The accused is made answerable for knowledge rather than simply asked to look.
findings.containment: Retains only the local rhetorical echo; the focus verb remains knowing and no direct wording identity is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The supplied evidence supports a bounded local relation while explicitly narrowing its broader lexical or interpretive range.

findings.title: obvious fact is posed as examination
findings.claim: The fact that God sees is posed as an examination of a subject who should acknowledge it.
findings.mechanism: The matrix interrogative is rhetorical rather than information-seeking, so it tests the subject's response to an available fact.
findings.reader_payoff: Culpability enters before the asserted content is completed.
findings.containment: The question still asks whether he knows; the examination force supplements that plain sense.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology, syntax, sound, or local relation directly supports the bounded finding.

findings.title: knowing should already have occurred
findings.claim: The opening treats the missing knowledge as knowledge already due.
findings.mechanism: {ar:لَمْ, tr:lam, gloss:olumsuz geçmiş} governs the jussive {ar:يَعْلَمْ, tr:yaʿlam, gloss:bilmek}, giving the failure a completed and accountable shape.
findings.reader_payoff: The rebuke reaches backward to an established lapse rather than a neutral present gap.
findings.containment: This is a particle effect, not a claim that the verb itself is past tense.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology, syntax, sound, or local relation directly supports the bounded finding.

findings.title: negative question becomes rebuke
findings.claim: The negative question functions as a rebuke expecting acknowledgment of what should be known.
findings.mechanism: The interrogative hamza and jussive negation jointly govern the cognition clause, converting negated knowing into a directed challenge.
findings.reader_payoff: The first words sound like a demand for recognition, not a survey of ignorance.
findings.containment: The negative interrogative remains a question in form; its rebuking force is the added relation.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology, syntax, sound, or local relation directly supports the bounded finding.

findings.title: one question binds knowing to seeing

findings.mechanism: The {ar:بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ, tr:bi-anna llāha yarā, gloss:Allah'ın gördüğü} clause is attached as the content of {ar:يَعْلَمْ, tr:yaʿlam, gloss:bilmek} under the opening question.
findings.reader_payoff: The charge is heard as failure to know this particular reality: that God sees.
findings.containment: The supplied attachment is retained; the content clause is not detached into a second claim.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology, syntax, sound, or local relation directly supports the bounded finding.

findings.title: verb pivots rebuke into content

findings.mechanism: The cognition verb stands between the negative interrogative and the compound connector, routing the accusation into a demanded act of knowing.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader knows exactly what the accused is charged with failing to hold in awareness.
